blocks.title: Velocity selector
blocks.text: A velocity selector is a device used to determine the velocity of a charged particle. In it, electric and magnetic forces are applied to the moving particle in such a way that they balance each other only for one value of velocity, allowing the particle to continue moving with a constant velocity.

Consider a particle with a positive charge +q that enters a uniform magnetic field B at a right angle to it with a velocity v. The magnetic force acts on the particle in the upward direction (Fig. 10.11). To balance this magnetic force, an electric force must act downward on the particle.

A velocity selector consists of a cylindrical tube located within a magnetic field B. Inside the tube is a parallel plate capacitor that creates a uniform electric field E, oriented perpendicular to the magnetic field B (Fig. 10.12). When the charged particle enters the left end of the tube, the magnetic force acts upward while the electric force acts downward, in the direction of E, on the positively charged particle. If the strengths of the electric and magnetic fields are adjusted appropriately, these forces cancel each other out. With no net force acting on the particle, its velocity v remains constant in accordance with Newton's first law; the particle moves in a straight line at constant velocity and exits the right end of the tube. Particles with velocities different from v are deflected and do not exit at the right end.

The magnitude of the velocity selected follows directly. As v is perpendicular to both B and E, the magnetic force (upward) is Bqv and the electric force (downward) is qE. For no deflection of the particle, Bqv = qE, or v = E/B ... (10.15).

blocks.title: Example 10.4
blocks.text: Alpha particles ranging in speed from 1000 m s^-1 to 2000 m s^-1 enter a velocity selector where the electric intensity is 300 V m^-1 and the magnetic induction is 0.20 T. Which particles will move undeviated through the field? Solution: E = 300 V m^-1 = 300 N C^-1, B = 0.20 T. Only those particles pass for which the electric force qE balances the magnetic force Bqv (Fig. 10.12): qE = Bqv, so v = E/B = 300 N C^-1/0.20 N A^-1 m^-1 = 1500 m s^-1. The alpha particles with speed 1500 m s^-1 move undeviated.

blocks.title: Example 10.5
blocks.text: A charged particle moves through a velocity selector at constant velocity in a straight line. The electric field of the selector is 4.8 x 10^3 N C^-1 and the magnetic field is 0.2 T. When the electric field is turned off, the particle travels on a circular path of radius 3.0 cm. Find the charge to mass ratio of the particle. Solution: as the particle moves perpendicular to both E and B, qE = Bqv and v = E/B. With the electric field off, the magnetic force provides the centripetal force: Bqv = mv^2/r, so q/m = v/(Br). Putting v = E/B, q/m = E/(B^2 r) = 4.8 x 10^3 N C^-1/((0.2 T)^2 x 3 x 10^-2 m) = 4 x 10^6 C kg^-1.

A force is exerted on a charged particle moving in a magnetic field. In what direction should it move so that no force is exerted on it? Along the field lines, since then theta = 0 and qvB sin theta = 0 (Point to ponder).

blocks.prompt: What is a velocity selector? Explain its working (comprehensive question 10.5). A particle moves undeflected through a selector at 4.96 x 10^4 m s^-1 with B = 0.114 T; what electric field is needed (numerical 10.11, printed 7.11)?
blocks.explanation: It is a region where a uniform electric field and a uniform magnetic field act at right angles to each other and to the beam; the electric force qE and the magnetic force Bqv on a moving charge are opposite, and they cancel only when v = E/B, so only particles of that speed pass straight through while faster or slower ones are deflected. E = vB = 4.96 x 10^4 x 0.114 = 5.65 x 10^3 N C^-1.

items: Velocity selector: crossed E (capacitor plates) and B; for +q the magnetic force Bqv is up and the electric force qE down; they balance only when v = E/B (10.15); that particle goes straight (Newton's first law), others are deflected.
Example 10.4: 1500 m s^-1 passes. Example 10.5: q/m = E/(B^2 r) = 4 x 10^6 C kg^-1.
